defects: MINOR hotkeys.py:404-413 (N2 rule as written in the T21 spec). A swallowed Alt-combo key that is physically held but produces no auto-repeat is treated as released after 1.2 s, and a held hold-to-talk session stops by itself. Measured with the real App: ask LeftAlt+VK0x86 without repeats stopped at 1.296 s (held until 3.03 s); dictate LeftAlt+VK0x87 stopped at 1.265 s. Sources without repeats include mouse buttons or macro software (G Hub, AutoHotkey remaps) mapped to F13-F24, which are the likely way to produce VK0x86/0x87, and FilterKeys with repeat turned off. The same happens when the user presses any other key while holding the combo, because Windows then repeats only that key (state-machine sim: Space released and stop emitted 1.2 s after its last repeat). Under T20 these keys were never sampled as physically down and were never dropped, so this is a regression for those setups. Normal keyboards are unaffected (checked down to the slowest 1.0 s delay / 0.4 s rate). The default combos are modifier-only, except dictate 'Alt+Shift+Space', whose Space repeats. Suggested direction: apply the timeout only after at least one auto-repeat was seen, or use a much longer timeout when no repeat was ever seen.

NIT desktop.py:521-524. A non-integer hotkeys_version in a hand-edited settings.json (for example "2") raises TypeError in migrate_hotkeys (hotkeys.py:95). The load try block only catches OSError/ValueError, so App construction fails (reproduced: TypeError("'>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'")).

NIT hotkeys.py:389,419 (accepted trade-off of the spec). If the real key-up of a synthetically released key is lost (for example on a hook timeout), the key is not sampled again until it is pressed again. Until then the ask session keeps recording and deferred pastes wait. This mirrors the T12 never-seen rule.

NIT scripts/check_wave_d.py:240-256. ask_stop_seconds_after_press reports the release time when no stop occurred during the hold, so it is not a measured stop time; the boolean checks are still correct.
NIT scripts/check_hotkey_hook.py has no swallowed-key-stuck scenario (optional per acceptance); covered by the auditor's real MARKER-lost-key-up check.
